description: R2D, the Regional Resilience Determination tool, creates and launches simulation workflows that estimate the regional damage and loss from natural hazard events for inventories of buildings and civil infrastructure. It is developed by the NSF-funded NHERI SimCenter, led by Frank McKenna at UC Berkeley with Stevan Gavrilovic, Jinyan Zhao, Kuanshi Zhong, Adam Zsarnoczay and others; the documentation read covers version 5.5, and example files for earlier releases are archived on Zenodo. The rWHALE backend chains applications that build inventories, characterise hazards and simulate damage and loss, and users can swap in their own applications; runs are local or on DesignSafe high-performance computers. Coverage: scenario or probabilistic assessments of hurricanes, earthquakes and other hazards anywhere with inventory data; example 10 covers about 14,000 buildings and 177 soil sites in Alameda, California. Access: installers and source on GitHub, documentation online. Licence: BSD 3-Clause; free. Caveats: results depend on the chosen inventory and damage models, and the tool is under active development. Simulation uses: regional seismic and hurricane loss, community impact and recovery studies. Related records: pelicun, IN-CORE and the Los Angeles woodframe case study.
